transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Dalia Rivera (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Tom Chen (HavenTech Head of ML), Sarah Lopez (HavenTech CTO), Randy Morgan (HavenTech Lead DevOps)

Summary (auto): QBR health check covering usage, cost, reliability, and next steps for a Dedicated pilot. Action items captured.

[00:00] Dalia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is the QBR health check, I'm Dalia from Redwood. we've got Marcus and Priya with me. can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Tom: yeah hi Tom here, Head of ML at HavenTech. we've been ramping usage for the last two quarters.
[00:18] Sarah: Sarah, CTO, i'll be on for the first half, then i've got another call.
[00:23] Randy: Randy, infra lead, i'll stick around for the infra/security bits.
[00:28] Marcus: Marcus Lee, SE for Redwood, i'll cover latency / benchmark stuff and Dedicated sizing.
[00:34] Priya: Priya Nair, CSM, i'm tracking adoption and the contract milestones.
[00:40] Dalia: great. quick agenda: usage/cost trends, reliability (errors/latency), security checklist, and roadmap + next steps.

[02:05] Dalia: Tom, can you start with a high-level on how you're using the API and what the growth looks like?
[02:15] Tom: sure, main use is customer support assistant, plus an internal r&d summarization pipeline. we're at about 4M tokens/month now, up from 2.1M three months ago. cost is start-- we're seeing the token bill creep up, right. single-digit percent growth month over month but the cost per query is becoming a focus.
[02:38] Randy: and we've seen a few production incidents where p99 latency spikes to 600ms during peak, usually correlated with longer context prompts.
[02:46] Marcus: okay that aligns with what we saw on our end for similar workloads - longer contexts can push kernel switching and cache misses. We've got a couple of levers: smarter batching, prefix KV caching, and quantization profiles to lower compute.

[05:10] Sarah: can you remind me of what Dedicated gives us versus hosted - like latency SLOs and isolation?
[05:18] Dalia: yes, Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, region pinning, and improved p99 stability. it also gives isolated tenancy so data retention is simpler for compliance. SLA-backed uptime typically 99.9% depending on tier.
[05:35] Sarah: and on costs? we have a fixed commit model?
[05:40] Dalia: Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit pricing — usually more predictable unit economics. we can model a break-even point vs hosted depending on steady-state tokens and peak throughput. Marcus can run the sizing sim.

[07:12] Marcus: quick note — if you have lots of short chat-like prompts, continuous KV cache and lighter quantization is better. for long-doc summarization the model footprint increases so batching and 4-bit quantization profiles show big savings.
[07:30] Tom: are there quality tradeoffs with 4-bit? we've been wary of any drop in summary quality.
[07:36] Marcus: small quality delta for many workloads; we recommend AB evals on a few hundred prompts to measure. we'll run that for you.

[09:50] Tom: on error rates, we've seen an uptick of 0.9% 5xxs in the last 30 days. is that on your side or ours?
[09:58] Marcus: we'll correlate traces but often 5xxs at that scale are transient overloads at bursting times or network retries. Router config and automatic fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant can keep things flowing. do you have tracing turned on?
[10:14] Randy: we send trace IDs but not full distributed tracing into Redwood yet; security wanted to minimize PII.
[10:22] Priya: we can share instructions for safe tracing redaction and sample rate configs.

[12:40] Dalia: i'd like to show the usage dashboard quickly — (screen share) — OK see the last 90/180 day trends, tokens by route, and cost per model. notice the growth in the support-assistant route.
[12:58] Sarah: yeah that visual helps. can you export the CSV so finance can run the numbers?
[13:05] Dalia: absolutely, i'll attach the CSV in the follow-up email.

[15:30] Tom: roadmap wise, are there upcoming infra changes that might help p99? we heard something about improved KV cache and smarter routing?
[15:40] Marcus: correct — roadmap items include a new workload-aware routing engine that can route by latency or cost preference at request time, improved KV cache hit rates for multi-turn chat, and more aggressive batching heuristics. expected gradual rollout over Q3.
[15:58] Tom: timeline?
[16:00] Marcus: beta for workload-aware routing in late August, KV cache improvements rolling through September. we'll invite you to early access.

[18:22] Randy: security/compliance — need to get SOC2 and ISO docs, and KMS integration details. also curious about audit logs retention for Dedicated.
[18:30] Priya: we have a SOC2 package and ISO summary; Dalia will share the links. Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS with HSM options, and audit logs retention is configurable, typical 90/365 day options depending on plan.
[18:48] Sarah: good. we'll need a contact for legal procurement.
[18:51] Dalia: i'll cc our legal and security contact in the follow-up and share the procurement checklist.

[21:10] Tom: wanted to surface one problem — during a high-traffic promotion last month a route throttled and some partner calls failed. it seems rate-limiter thresholds were hit. any suggestions?
[21:22] Marcus: we can tune token rate limits per API key, and Dedicated gives higher baseline throughput with burst capacity. also pre-warming and scheduled capacity increases for promotions is a common pattern. we can add a canary policy to traffic.

[24:00] Dalia: quick pricing discussion — based on your 4M tokens/month, hosted costs are roughly X per token (redacted in meeting), Dedicated could bring unit cost down by ~20-35% depending on commit. we'll provide a modeled comparison in the deck.
[24:24] Sarah: finance will want the model assumptions spelled out.
[24:27] Dalia: yes, we'll show pricing per-million tokens, assumed utilization, and amortized infra.

[27:15] Marcus: on benchmarking, i'll run an 8k prompt average workload and measure p50/p90/p99 and throughput on a Dedicated-equivalent node, then compare to your hosted baseline.
[27:26] Tom: that'd be helpful, include memory/KV cache hits so we can see root cause.

[30:40] Randy: on network and VPC, if we go Dedicated we need VPC peering and static egress IPs for allowlist. how does that work?
[30:50] Dalia: Dedicated supports VPC peering and egress IP configuration; we'll include the network design doc. also for on-prem/private we have a package but that's a bigger lift.

[33:15] Priya: follow-up timeline: Dalia will send QBR deck and CSV (due 7/16), Marcus will run benchmark (7/21), Priya will schedule Dedicated pilot kickoff (week of 7/27).

[35:00] Sarah: any blockers on our end? I think procurement will need the SOC2 and contract terms.
[35:08] Dalia: we'll include a draft contract and a procurement checklist in the follow-up.

[38:45] Tom: quick question about model version pinning — if we pin to a Redwood-verified model, how do rollouts work?
[38:54] Marcus: you can pin and do canary rollouts; the console supports route-level rollouts with automatic fallback policies if quality/regression thresholds are exceeded. there are eval hooks you can attach to your prompt set.

[42:20] Randy: what's the expected p99 improvement if we move to Dedicated? any numbers?
[42:28] Marcus: based on similar customers, p99 improved from ~450-600ms down to 180-250ms in steady state, subject to prompt length. we'll confirm after the benchmark.

[45:00] Sarah: if we want to proceed with a pilot, what's the earliest start?
[45:08] Dalia: we can typically spin a pilot in 2-3 weeks after SOW and onboarding; list of contacts and network details will speed it up.

[48:30] Tom: one more thing — we'd like a short eval run to compare quality between quantized and full-precision models.
[48:38] Marcus: we'll run AB evals on your anonymized prompts, show quality metrics (ROUGE/BLEU where appropriate, human-check flags), and share results.

[51:00] Dalia: recap of next steps and action items — read them out loud?
[51:10] Priya: sure. Dalia to share QBR deck, CSV, SOC2/ISO links, and procurement checklist by 2026-07-16. Marcus to run benchmark and AB evals and share results by 2026-07-21. Priya to schedule Dedicated pilot kickoff for week of 2026-07-27. Tom to provide anonymized prompt set by 2026-07-17.
[52:05] Sarah: that sounds right. thanks everyone.
[52:10] Dalia: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and add calendar invites.
[52:20] Tom: thanks. bye.

End of transcript.
